frame: x east along the front, y up from the terrace's foot at the hall's box, z south (out of the front, towards 大水法); the origin on 大水法's axis at the wings' front plane; metres

terr_w.note: the terrace W-E: S603's 'about 31 m' taken W-E (plate 14 draws the side rails about 30 m apart, c); order not stated (Q67)

terr_d.note: the terrace N-S: S603's 35 m; its south face meets 大水法's model (models/XY10-da-shuifa/, the stairs' landings)

terr_y.note: the terrace's top above its foot: 大水法's stairs arrive 4.63 m above the court (Round 15, Q232); the court lies 0.33 m below this box's ground

pier_step.note: the retaining walls' piers ('monolithic piers with long rusticated stones', S603 p.131-132): their spacing assumed

front_rail_x.note: the straight front balustrade's ends, where it turns back north: plate 14 x 744-1661 at the rail's depth; 大水法's stairs arrive beyond them

hall_w.note: the hall W-E: S603's 28 m (the post grid); the rubble core 28.4 m W-E (S850, b); plate 14's wings and centre at the 6.0 m column spacing make 27-28 m, against 18 m at 4.2 m (Q67)

hall_d.note: the hall N-S: S603's 21 m; the rubble core N-S 20.1 m (S850, b)

S.note: the carved columns' spacing, the module of the front: plate 14's own ratios against S603's 28 m (the centre 431 px, the columns 228 px apart, the wings 200 px) and P0216's door (the column 3.0 m off the door's axis at a 2.0 m door); the dossier's 4.2 m (the 'centre bays 4 m', c) gives an 18 m front. P0183's brick courses then 10.6 cm

base_h.note: the hall's floor above the terrace: the door's and the side openings' jambs stop at the pedestals' top on P0216 and P0757 (reader 2); plate 14 a raised base and the threshold 41 px above the pedestals' foot

wing_w.note: each wing over its outer side face and the centre block's corner: 28 m less the centre; its front face 5.0 m, plate 14's 200 px at 40 px/m (the 28 m on 1125 px)

wing_ch.note: the wings' chamfered corners, outer and inner: plate 14, facets of 35-41 px with their own pilasters (reader 1); S603's 'eight-slope' wing roofs fit a chamfered plan

wing_d.note: each wing's depth as a pavilion under its own roof: assumed; the body runs on behind

recess.note: how far the centre block stands back of the wings' front: the wing's inner face holds one window bay (plate 14, reader 1: 0.7-0.9 of the wing's front); S310 '倒凹'

ctr_w.note: the centre block's front: P0183's pier between column and side opening 0.27 S (the openings' axes 5.6 m out, P0183, P0216, P0719 all put them 1 m further out than v2's 4.75 m); plate 14 draws that pier 0.12 S

ctr_d.note: the centre block's depth under its tiered roof: assumed, about square as plate 14 draws the main roof

band_h.note: the low band over the centre block's cornice, under the fish-scale roof: plate 14 (the roof's eave about 1 m over the cornice at the attic's scrolls)

cornice.note: the main cornice's and the entablature blocks' top above the terrace: P0183 1.34 S (the photographs; plate 14 draws the order short, 1.11-1.27 S: trust the photographs, reader 1)

col_ped.note: the pedestals' top, on the floor's level: P0216, P0757 (0.17-0.21 of the shaft and capital, reader 2)

col_top.note: the capitals' top above the pedestals' foot: P0183 1.19 S; P0216 1.74 times the door's height

col_r.note: the shaft's radius: shaft and capital 6.5-6.7 shaft widths (P0216, P0757, reader 2)

cap_h.note: the capital: 0.24 of the shaft and capital (P0216, reader 2), a Corinthian type with a mask (P0183)

blk_w.note: the entablature block: 2.5-2.8 shaft widths wide, standing proud of the wall (reader 2)

col_d.note: the columns' axis before the wall: each stands before a plain pier bonded into the wall, its block projecting deeply (P0179, P0216, P0291, reader 2)

door_w.note: the door's opening: P0183 0.32 S (reader 1), P0216 2.0 m at the plate's figure (reader 2)

door_h.note: the door's opening above the floor to its arch's crown: its head 0.90 S above the pedestals' foot (P0183)

cwin_w.note: the centre block's side openings: door-like, to the floor, 1.65 x 4.0 m, their crowns level with the door's (P0216, P0179, reader 2)

cwin_x.note: the side openings' axes: P0183's pier between column and opening 0.27 S (reader 1); v2's 4.75 m sat 1 m inside on P0183, P0216 and P0719

win_w.note: the wings' windows: plate 14, 0.25 x 0.65 of the wing's front, on a carved sill block 0.23 of it above the foot

win_sill.note: the wings' window sills above the terrace: on a carved sill block 0.23 Wf above the wing's foot on the base (plate 14); v2's 1.35 m sat 1.6 m low on the plate

clock_y.note: the clock wheel's centre above the terrace: 1.61 S on P0183, 1.60 on plate 14: the attic agrees on both

clock_r.note: the wheel's radius: P0183 0.25 S across, plate 14 0.31 S

attic_w.note: the attic between its pilasters' outer faces: P0183, 230 of 446 px

scroll_x.note: the attic's foot scrolls' tips either side of the axis: P0183 1.17 S, plate 14 1.09 S over their span

skirt_top.note: the fish-scale roof from a low band over the cornice to the main roof's foot: plate 14 draws its eave tips 2 m over the cornice (1.63 against 1.24 Wf), a band with the attic's scrolls between

roof_eave.note: the main hipped roof's eave: plate 14, its corner tips (lifted) level with the attic's arch, 2.08 Wf

roof_w.note: the main roof over its eave tips: plate 14, 359 px (1.57 S)

roof_apex.note: the main roof's top: plate 14, 2.50 Wf (2.19 S); the dossier's 12.4 m on the old 2 m base and a 4.2 m column spacing

crown.note: the crown's top: plate 14, 2.92 Wf (2.56 S); box XY09-M44 had 12.6 m above the terrace

lan_w.note: the lanterns' width: plate 14, 0.4 of the wing's front

lan_foot.note: the deck under the lantern, its balustrade's top 9.3 m (plate 14, 1.60 Wf)

lan_clock.note: the lantern's clock centre: plate 14, 1.77 Wf; the face 0.26 Wf across

lan_top.note: the lantern's urn finial: plate 14, 2.45 Wf

body_ridge.note: the body behind under a hipped Chinese roof (S603 p.133: side bays two-slope Chinese tile, B): its ridge assumed; plate 14 shows only low roofs behind the wings, below the centre's main roof and the lanterns (v3's 12.0 m competed with the centre's tiers in the overlay)

trees.note: the forecourt's trees: plate 14, four a side in a row running outward, the innermost in line with the wings' inner faces; none before the centre
